results.claim: THEORY.md, R1: unknown ellipsoid, deterministic relative Gaussian mass enclosure

human: Gilbert, Kuo and Sloan, arXiv:2112.11621, Theorem 1 and conclusion
Rademacher and Vempala, arXiv:cs/0608054, Theorem 2 (volume) and the discussion in the introduction
comparison.explanation: An oracle upper bound with logarithmic precision dependence for nonmonotone, translated Gaussian ellipsoids; this neither negates the Cartesian singularity theorem nor improves the Lebesgue-volume lower bound for parallelepipeds.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R2: nonadaptive precision lower bound for nested Gaussian balls

human: Rademacher and Vempala, arXiv:cs/0608054, Theorem 23 (nonadaptive lower bound), Section 5.1
comparison.explanation: A randomized nonadaptive Omega(1/epsilon) lower bound uniform in dimension on a nested Gaussian ball family. The cited lower bound concerns dimensional dependence at fixed accuracy for volume and a much broader convex-body class.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R3: inverse-rarity lower bound with adaptive randomized point queries

human: Rademacher and Vempala, arXiv:cs/0608054, Theorems 2 (volume) and 23 (nonadaptive lower bound)
comparison.explanation: For Gaussian balls of unknown location with uniformly comparable small masses, any randomized adaptive method needs order inverse mass at constant relative precision. The volume result concerns well-rounded bodies with a supplied common interior ball and dimensional rather than rarity dependence.

results.claim: THEORY.md, R4: two-coordinate preintegration for elliptical sections and stratified variance

human: Gilbert, Kuo and Sloan, arXiv:2112.11621, Theorem 1 and conclusion
He and Wang, doi:10.1137/15M1007963, Theorems 3.5 and 3.6; He, arXiv:1702.03361, Proposition 2.3
comparison.explanation: A global Lipschitz bound through quadratic tangencies and a variance of order n^(-1-2/(d-2)) after integrating two known Gaussian coordinates. This improves the directly applicable generic discontinuity exponent on the structured subclass, but the method and hypotheses differ from direct scrambled-net results.
